pillar_reactions.evidence: Pre-sold before the pitch started and said so — 'nobody needs to sell me on what you guys are doing like I already get it.' He identified the differentiator himself from the content: 'the very first video I saw of him with a dumbbell talking about stabilizing and your stomach and I just said this guy knows exactly what he's talking about', 'I've never seen anybody doing a full body workout and doing everything that he's doing', and on the mobility-first framing, 'Yeah, which is what I like, which I saw right away, for sure.' He has saved roughly 80% of Trevor's videos and shared them with six people.

Asked the same question three times and never got a clean answer. 'does he say, like, well, John's 220 as opposed to some guy who's 170 who wants to lose 10 pounds... does he give you an idea of these are the calories you should do a day?' and then 'So he's not like, here are your macros, 20, 80?' The rep's answer was audibly unresolved — 'I want to say it's like a hybrid between like, like keto and something else, but... I'm to think of the word' — and he eventually deferred it to Trevor. The prospect then misheard the protocol entirely and had to check: 'Did you say he's having people only eat once a day?', corrected to 'Cooking only one main meal a day'.

Understood and valued the video form-review mechanism without needing to be convinced — 'obviously you take videos of yourself and you send it and if he needs to correct it, I was like, wow, that's good. You know, a lot of the things that he was saying that he does, I'm like, man, nobody does that.' No questions on mechanics and no pushback. Notably he did not treat accountability as his gap — he positions himself as already disciplined ('I'm like a disciplined person', 'I'll get up at three o'clock in the morning if I need to'), so the pillar the offer charges most for is the one he values least.

anchors.raw: I don't know, that comes down to like $150 a week, roughly. So if you go out there and look for a personal trainer, you're probably going to spend more than that on a personal trainer. That's probably going to do less for you.
anchors.note: The prospect built the value case himself and he is a salesman who knows the market — 'that's, I said before, I know numbers. Cause I've tried to work with trainers before and they want to charge a lot more money.' He also volunteered the credentialing critique: 'I studied and I took that ISSA exam and I got a certificate. I paid $800 for a weekend, I'm like an expert.' The price was never the problem. The cashflow was.

anchors.raw: I'm going to do this or not with him or without him. ... If he says no, I'm going to just mimic the videos and do every single thing I can. ... I guarantee that if I do 90% of everything that he has by watching videos, it's probably going to do what I want to do anyway.
anchors.competitor: Trevor's own free Instagram and YouTube content
anchors.note: The most dangerous anchor in the corpus so far because the competitor is the company's own marketing. He has saved roughly 80% of the library and already owns three kettlebells. The rep conceded rather than contested it. For a prospect with bilateral rotator cuff tears the 90% claim is also clinically wrong, and that argument was available and unused.

anchors.raw: It's more than a car payment, but I think what I might do is I might put money aside for, you know, a couple of months
anchors.note: He benchmarks the monthly figure against a car payment and a mortgage, not against coaching. His stated ceiling is $350, 'maybe four', against a $650 floor on the six-month tier and $433 on the improvised three-month tier — so every option presented sat above the line he had drawn.

anchors.raw: I'm on flat commission, I have no base salary... so I just went, like, two months, like, February, March, I didn't have a sale, so that's my point, it's a little tough, if I was on a base salary, I'd easily be like, oh, no problem
anchors.note: He named the precise condition that would flip him: 'Right now, if I had a base salary of $60,000 and I was making my commission, this conversation with the links that you're sending me, I wouldn't be having this. I would already have signed up.' He is actively job-hunting for exactly that. This is a genuine affordability constraint, not a value objection, and it is the one thing the payment plan could not stretch far enough to solve.

anchors.raw: I have three kettlebells downstairs and I've had them for, I don't know, three years. I've never used them though.
anchors.note: Bought the equipment three years ago and never used it — the cleanest possible proof that information and equipment without instruction produce nothing for him. Never used as an argument.

unmet_demand.want: A credible answer to whether loaded kettlebell work is safe and possible for someone with all three rotator cuff tendons torn off both shoulders, fatty muscle atrophy and a possible shoulder replacement ahead
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This was the reason for the call — 'I don't know if he can help me' — and it was answered with reassurance rather than assessment. The person answering had been on the team just over a month, is a self-described kettlebell beginner, and no clinician was involved on either side. The programme may or may not be able to accommodate it; nobody established which.

unmet_demand.want: Financing over 18 to 24 months at roughly $350/month
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep referenced splitting 'up to two years' in passing but every live option landed above the ceiling: $650/month on the six-month tier and $433/month on the improvised three-month tier, both over 12 months with interest. Nothing at or below $350 exists except the $199/month self-serve product, which is a different thing entirely.

unmet_demand.want: A calorie or portion target calibrated to his weight and rate of loss, given he is on a GLP-class peptide and worried about muscle loss
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Asked three times and never answered. The Primal Eating Protocol is positioned as deliberately non-quantitative ('you don't have to macro anything') and the rep could not say whether Trevor issues a calorie ceiling, guessing 'I'm sure he'll probably let me know, based on my age'. The programme may well handle it; nobody could say so.

unmet_demand.want: Confirmation before booking that the initial call would be with Trevor, or at minimum an honest answer about who and what was replying to his texts
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The booking flow answered 'let us get back to you to find out when Trevor's available' three or four times while auto-texting that his call was with Ben. He asked directly whether it was AI and never received an answer, including from the rep.

unmet_demand.want: Reassurance that the age range in Trevor's own introduction video does not exclude him
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Resolved on the call — the rep said clients are in their 60s — but the marketing asset still says 30 to 45 and the prospect nearly disqualified himself before speaking to anyone. A funnel problem, not an offer problem.
